na5d67ba3eca.s: Totemism among tribes goes with which marriage rule?
na5d67ba3eca.x: Members of a totem clan marry outside it, so totemism goes with clan exogamy, not endogamy.

ndd0ce61f5fd.x: The 75 PVTGs live in 18 States and one Union Territory, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

nf7b5e117186.s: PM-JANMAN of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs covers how many PVTGs?
nf7b5e117186.x: PM-JANMAN, with a ₹15,000 crore announcement, covers all 75 PVTGs.

n6407358cdf3.s: The Renke Commission on denotified tribes is associated with which year?
n6407358cdf3.x: The Renke Commission was in 2008; the Idate Commission followed in 2017 and the Criminal Tribes Inquiry Committee was in 1949.

o: The first tribal freedom fighter against the British
The first Scheduled Tribe President of India
The first anthropologist to study Indian tribes
The founder of the first tribal university
nindian-society-1-11.x: Tilka Manjhi was the first tribal freedom fighter against the British; Droupadi Murmu was the first ST President.

ndd2f9ae8255.s: Which scholar is associated with the primordialist view of ethnic identity?
ndd2f9ae8255.x: Geertz saw ethnic identity as given by birth in deep attachments; Brass is instrumentalist and Barth's boundary view is constructivist.

n312922a518d.s: How many mother tongues did the 2011 Census record?
n312922a518d.x: The 2011 Census recorded 121 languages and 270 mother tongues.

n2ca1531863f.s: Khasi, an official language of Meghalaya, belongs to which language group?
n2ca1531863f.x: Khasi is Austro-Asiatic (Mon-Khmer); Garo is the one in the Bodo group of the Sino-Tibetan family.

n043a86a77b7.s: Which of the following (year – reorganisation) is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2019 – Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories
1966 – Punjab/Haryana reorganisation, Chandigarh made a UT
n043a86a77b7.x: Nagaland was formed in 1963; 1966 was the Punjab/Haryana reorganisation.

n58653f445b0.x: The term comes from European minority-rights law; it denotes a non-dominant citizen group with its own ethnic, religious or linguistic identity.

nc5917e0979e.s: The Tripura ethnic conflict is between:
nc5917e0979e.x: The Tripura conflict developed between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers after demographic change.

n05b93cafe8c.s: Which approach treats ethnic groups as interest groups competing unequally for power and resources?
n05b93cafe8c.x: The conflict approach sees groups competing unequally (e.g. South Africa, Sri Lankan Tamils); the consensus approach sees them coexisting.

ncaa70380947.s: A low caste or tribe adopting the customs, rituals and way of life of a higher, twice-born caste to claim higher rank is called:
ncaa70380947.x: This is Srinivas's definition of Sanskritisation.

n6ddca4e3bd2.s: Which process comes specifically from the West/British, unlike a universal process?
n6ddca4e3bd2.x: Westernisation is source-specific, while modernisation is a universal process that may come from any source.

nindian-society-8-30.s: The spread of culture through the media is called:
nindian-society-8-30.x: The media creates awareness, forms public opinion and contributes to cultural diffusion, the spread of culture.

nindian-society-4-10.s: Taking part in the wider society while retaining one's own identity is called:
nindian-society-4-10.x: Integration is participation while keeping identity; assimilation is absorption into the dominant culture.

nindian-society-2-13.s: Who wrote 'The Aborigines So-Called and Their Future', which argued for tribal assimilation?
nindian-society-2-13.x: Ghurye wrote it and argued for tribal assimilation; Elwin wrote The Tribal World of Verrier Elwin.

ndc38d563651.s: Who wrote 'The Passing of Traditional Society' (1958)?
ndc38d563651.x: Daniel Lerner wrote it; When a Great Tradition Modernizes is by Milton Singer.

new.s: How many individual ethnic groups are notified as Scheduled Tribes in India (Census 2011 count)?
new.x: 705 ethnic groups are notified as STs in 30 States/UTs.

new.s: How many communities are notified as Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has 34 notified STs; 12 is the PVTG count of the joint AP-Telangana list.

new.s: After which Act are ST lists revised by later amendment orders?
new.x: ST lists are revised by later amendment orders after the SC and ST Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976.

new.s: Under Article 342(2), who can include or exclude a community from the ST list?
new.x: Article 342(1) lets the President notify STs; under 342(2) only Parliament, by law, can amend the list.

new.s: The first order notifying Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(1) was issued in:
new.x: The first order was the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.

new.s: Which State/UT has the highest percentage of ST population (Census 2011)?
new.x: Lakshadweep has 94.8%, just ahead of Mizoram at 94.4%.

new.s: Which State has the largest Scheduled Tribe population by number (Census 2011)?
new.x: Madhya Pradesh has about 1.53 crore STs, about 21% of India's STs.

new.s: Which is the largest tribe of India?
new.x: Bhil is the largest tribe; Gond is second.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (tribe – State/UT) is wrongly matched?
new.x: The Onge live in the Andaman Islands, not Lakshadweep.

new.s: The Chenchus of Andhra Pradesh live mainly in the Nallamala forests of:
new.x: The Chenchus are hunters and food-gatherers of the Nallamala forests in Kurnool, Prakasam and Guntur.

new.s: Which tribe of Andhra Pradesh lives mainly in the north hills of Srikakulam and Vizianagaram?
new.x: Savara, Jatapu, Gadaba and Konda Dora live in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram; Koya are in the Godavari valley.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (AP tribe – habitat) is wrongly matched?
o: Konda Reddi – East and West Godavari
new.x: Yanadi and Yerukula are plains tribes; the Nallamala forests are the home of the Chenchus.

new.s: The 'Morung' youth dormitory is associated with the:
new.x: Morung belongs to the Nagas; Dhumkuria is Oraon and Ghotul is Muria Gond.

new.s: Who classified the Jarawa and Onge as Negrito?
new.x: B.S. Guha's racial classification put Jarawa and Onge in the Negrito group.

new.s: Gond, Oraon (Kurukh) and Khond (Kui) belong to which linguistic group?
new.x: Gond, Oraon and Khond are Dravidian; Santhal and Munda are Austro-Asiatic.

new.s: Shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation in North-East India is called:
new.x: Shifting cultivation is called Jhum in North-East India; the others are youth dormitories.

new.s: Animism refers to:
o: Belief in and worship of nature spirits
A clan's mystic bond with a totem
new.x: Animism is belief in and worship of nature spirits; the mystic bond with a totem is totemism.

new.s: In which year was the Primitive Tribal Group (PTG) category created?
new.x: PTGs were created in 1973 and renamed PVTGs in 2006; the Dhebar Commission sat in 1960-61.

new.s: Which State has the highest number of PVTGs?
new.x: Odisha has 13 PVTGs, the highest; AP with Telangana has 12 and Bihar 9.

new.s: How many of the 12 PVTGs of the joint list belong to residual Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Kolam and Thoti are on the Telangana side, leaving 10 in residual Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: Which is the largest PVTG by population?
new.x: Sahariyas are the largest PVTG; Sentinelese and Andamanese are the smallest.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-JANMAN:
1. It was launched on 15 November 2023, Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
2. Its approved outlay is ₹24,104 crore.
3. It is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong because PM-JANMAN is a Ministry of Tribal Affairs mission.

new.s: After the Criminal Tribes Act was repealed in 1952, it was replaced by:
o: The SC and ST Orders (Amendment) Act
new.x: The Act was repealed on 31 August 1952 and replaced by State Habitual Offenders Acts.

new.s: The All India Criminal Tribes Inquiry Committee (1949) is also known as the:
new.x: The 1949 committee is the Ayyangar Committee; Renke (2008) and Idate (2017) came later.

new.s: Denotified Tribes were last counted in which Census?
new.x: DNTs were last counted in Census 1931; the RGI has agreed to enumerate them in Census 2027.

new.s: 'The Bhils: A Study' was written by:
new.x: T.B. Naik wrote The Bhils: A Study.

new.s: The Shompen are protected by the A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation of which year?
new.x: The Shompen of Great Nicobar are protected by the A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956.

new.s: The Rohingya are a Sunni Muslim minority of:
new.x: The Rohingya of Rakhine State, Myanmar, are denied citizenship and are effectively stateless.

new.s: Which is China's largest Muslim group?
new.x: The Hui are China's largest Muslim group; China recognises 55 minority groups.

new.s: How many minority groups are officially recognised in China?
new.x: China has 55 recognised minority groups; the Han are over 91%.

new.s: Sixth Schedule autonomous district councils are provided under Article:
new.x: The Sixth Schedule (Art. 244(2)) gives autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – State) is wrongly matched?
new.x: Article 371C is for Manipur; Assam is under 371B.

new.s: The Inner Line Permit system dates from:
new.x: The Inner Line Permit dates from 1873.

new.s: Operation Blue Star (1984) was directed against which movement?
new.x: Blue Star was in Punjab against the Khalistan movement; Bajrang, Rhino and All Clear were against ULFA.

new.s: The Mizo National Front (MNF) was led by:
new.x: Laldenga led the MNF; Phizo led the NNC and Ghising the GNLF.

new.s: In which year was the State of Nagaland inaugurated?
new.x: The State of Nagaland Act was passed in 1962 and the state was inaugurated on 1 December 1963.

new.s: The Gorkhaland Territorial Administration was set up in:
new.x: The DGHC came in 1988 and the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration in 2012.

new.s: What is the cut-off date under the Assam Accord (1985) for detecting foreigners?
new.x: The Assam Accord with AASU/AAGSP fixed 24 March 1971 as the cut-off.

new.s: After the Mizo Accord of 1986, Mizoram became a State in:
new.x: The Mizo Accord was signed in 1986 and statehood followed in 1987.

new.s: Under the Bru-Reang Agreement (2020), the Brus were settled in:
new.x: The 2020 agreement of the Centre, Tripura and Mizoram settled the Brus in Tripura.

new.s: The ethnic conflict in Mizoram is between:
new.x: Mizoram's conflict is Mizo vs Bru; Meitei vs Kuki is Manipur.

new.s: Fredrik Barth's view that ethnic identity is kept by boundaries is called:
new.x: Barth (Ethnic Groups and Boundaries) is constructivist; Geertz is primordialist and Brass instrumentalist.

new.s: The Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival is associated with the:
new.x: The Nyishi, the largest tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, hold the Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival; Longpi pottery is Tangkhul Naga.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ethnicity and minority?
o: Giddens defined a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language
Intra-ethnic conflict takes place within a group
The consensus approach sees groups coexisting with separate identities
Language, religion, race, region and culture are markers of ethnicity
new.x: The race, nationality, religion or language definition is Arnold Rose's; Giddens stressed disadvantage, solidarity and isolation.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November of which year?
new.x: Andhra State came in 1953; the SRC led to the 1956 Act and Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956.

new.s: The concepts of Universalisation and Parochialisation were given by:
new.x: McKim Marriott gave universalisation (little to great) and parochialisation (great to little).

new.s: The concept of Great Tradition and Little Tradition was given by:
new.x: Redfield gave it; Milton Singer and McKim Marriott applied it to India.

new.s: In Marriott's terms, the flow of elements from the great tradition to the little tradition is:
new.x: Parochialisation is great to little; universalisation is little to great.

new.s: Constitutional secularism, with state neutrality and equal respect for religions, rests on Articles:
new.x: Constitutional secularism is a duty of the state under Articles 25-28.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about sociological secularisation:
1. It is the decline of religion's hold on social life.
2. It involves differentiation and rationalisation.
3. It is a duty of the state under the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 describes constitutional secularism, which is a duty of the state, not a change in society.

new.s: 'Modernization of Indian Tradition' (1973) was written by:
new.x: Yogendra Singh wrote it, studying change at macro and micro levels.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of modernisation?
new.x: Indicators of modernisation include rationality, scientific temper, industrialisation, urbanisation, literacy, mass media and democratic participation; hereditary occupation is not one.

new.s: Sanskritisation was first called:
new.x: Srinivas first called the process Brahminisation.

new.s: 'Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India', in which Sanskritisation was coined, appeared in:
new.x: Srinivas coined Sanskritisation in the Coorgs book of 1952.

new.s: Srinivas traced Westernisation to changes brought by:
new.x: Srinivas saw Westernisation as the change from 150+ years of British rule.

new.s: According to Srinivas, Westernisation is:
new.x: Srinivas preferred Westernisation as ethically neutral; modernisation is value-loaded.

new.s: 'Sensate and ideational cultures' are associated with:
new.x: Sorokin gave sensate/ideational cultures; Pareto gave circulation of elites.

new.s: The 'culture areas' idea belongs to which diffusionist school?
new.x: Culture areas = American school; culture circles = German-Austrian.

new.s: Durkheim's shift from mechanical to organic solidarity belongs to which theory of social change?
new.x: Durkheim is listed with Comte and Spencer among evolutionary theorists.

new.s: W.F. Ogburn's 'Social Change' was published in:
new.x: Ogburn set out cultural lag in Social Change (1922).

new.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, an example of law as a factor of social change, was passed in:
new.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act was passed in 1955.

new.s: In which process does a minority lose its distinct identity?
new.x: In assimilation the minority loses its identity; in acculturation it is influenced but stays distinct.
